item.title: Simon Helps Push Eastern Pacific Hurricane Activity to Record
item.description: The eastern Pacific has set a record for hurricane activity as Hurricane Simon lashes Mexico’s west coast and another storm threatens to form. The basin had produced 68.5 hurricane days as of Tuesday morning, surpassing the previous record of 68.25, according to Phil Klotzbach, a hurricane researcher at Colorado State University. “We should add several more hurricane days this week with Simon and very soon to be Trudy,” Klotzbach said by email.

item.title: 1MDB Has Proposal for Settlement With Deutsche Bank
item.description: has a proposal for settlement with Deutsche Bank AG in a $1.1 billion lawsuit, marking the latest potential resolution in the country’s long-running effort to recover money linked to the multibillion-dollar fraud. Related: Singapore’s DBS Faces $1 Billion Lawsuit in Alleged 1MDB-Linked Claim “We continue to feel strongly about our position in the case, which is supported by our particular fact pattern that is differentiated from other defendants, as well as recent developments in ongoing similar cases involving other parties,” said a spokesperson for Deutsche Bank. 1MDB started proceedings in Malaysia against Deutsche Bank’s local unit in 2021, claiming damages of $1.1 billion excluding interest, based on three wire transfers carried out by the unit in 2009 and 2011, according to the lender’s 2025 annual report.

item.title: Majority of Online Scam Campaigns Target Common Infrastructure: Study
item.description: Nearly 79% of online scam campaigns share at least one concrete indicator with another campaign, suggesting that seemingly unrelated scams often rely on common infrastructure. New research suggests scammers repeatedly exploit shared digital infrastructure, highlighting opportunities to disrupt multiple campaigns at once, according to cybersecurity firm ReasonLabs. “Most of these campaigns depend on infrastructure that can be identified across multiple scams.

item.title: Three arrests in major FCA operation against criminal insider dealing ring
item.description: The FCA has conducted a major operation to disrupt a suspected organised criminal group for engaging in insider dealing and money laundering. Steve Smart, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said: 'Insider dealing is a serious threat to the integrity of our markets. Working with partners, we will continue to use all the powers at our disposal to crack down on serious and organised crime groups engaged in market abuse.' In 2025/26, the FCA secured 4 insider dealing convictions, with 2 resulting in record sentences totalling 11 years of imprisonment.

item.title: Verisk estimates Hurricane Isaias insured onshore property losses in $1bn to $2bn range
item.description: Verisk, a catastrophe risk modelling and data analytics specialist, has now issued an initial industry insured loss estimate for recent hurricane Isaias, saying that onshore property losses from the storm could reach $2 billion. Verisk’s initial industry loss estimate includes losses from wind and privately insured storm surge, as a result of hurricane Isaias’ landfall in the Florida Panhandle. Cotality (formerly CoreLogic), estimated that insured losses from wind and storm surge from hurricane Isaias will be in the $2 billion to $3 billion range.

item.title: ILS investors need to speak up and ask for alternative model views: Karen Clark
item.description: At the ILS Bermuda Convergence 2026 conference today, Karen Clark, CEO and Co-founder of catastrophe risk modelling specialist Karen Clark & Company, urged the insurance-linked securities community and its investors to ask for alternative model views to be included in the deal flow that comes to market. “I think one of the things is, investors need to speak up that you do value alternative views, second generation models. During a panel discussion about how catastrophe modelling can be reimagined, Clark highlighted that ILS deal flow is typically concentrated around views of risk from the main vendor models.

item.title: Mid-single-digit billions of dollars loss from Isaias unlikely to affect P&C re/insurer credit profiles, says Fitch
item.description: A wide rage of insurers and reinsurers are expected to be impacted by Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall as a Category 2 storm in the Florida Panhandle on October 9th, but while the event is expected to drive moderate economic and insured losses, Fitch says it is “not likely to affect credit for rated property/casualty (P/C) (re)insurers.” Hurricane Isaias peaked as a Category 3 major hurricane over the Gulf before increasing wind shear weakened it on approach, eventually making landfall as a Category 2 storm with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph, although has now been downgraded to a tropical storm. In affected areas like Florida, Alabama, Georgia, and The Carolinas, Fitch expects the storm to result in moderate economic and insured losses, estimating that industry losses could reach the mid-single-digit billions of dollars. “The storm’s reduced intensity at landfall is expected to result in more manageable insured losses,” says Fitch.

item.title: Etude Launches E&S Carrier with $100M Surplus
item.description: Etude launched Etude Specialty Insurance Company, a technology-driven excess and surplus lines carrier for commercial property and casualty. Etude Specialty is domiciled in Nebraska, has more than $100 million of surplus, and will write in all 50 states. Using its own capital, with surplus currently in excess of $100 million, Etude Specialty can shape coverage, pricing, and policy language to solve complex insurance needs.

item.title: FAA Tells US Airlines to Exercise Caution in Saudi Arabia Flights, Citing Safety Risks
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration told US airlines to exercise caution when flying to or over Saudi Arabia, citing safety threats tied to ongoing military activities and navigation system interference. In September 2025, FedEx launched its first dedicated flight into Saudi Arabia. R iyadh airport remains closed to flights through at least 5 p.m.

item.title: Edison Drops on Willful Misconduct Allegations in Eaton Fire Case
item.description: Edison International shares fell over 3% on Tuesday after short seller Muddy Waters said it had uncovered new information suggesting the utility acted with “conscious” or “willful” disregard in the Eaton Fire. Related: Southern California Edison Chief Warns Wildfire Impasse Risks Higher Customer Bills The investment firm said Edison could face at least $4 billion in fire-related damages, with potential liability reaching about $20 billion if a court determines the firm’s conduct amounted to willful misconduct. item.title: Sammons introduces Criterion Wealth Management brand
item.description: Sammons Financial Group has introduced Criterion as the new name for its wealth advisory holding company, marking its continued expansion beyond insurance and annuities. Criterion brings together Beacon Capital Management, NorthRock Partners, and Wealthcare, which collectively have more than $27 billion in assets under management or advisement. item.title: Abacus partners with Retirable
item.description: Abacus Global Management has partnered with Retirable to connect clients with retirement planning services and integrate its LifeARC lifespan modeling technology into Retirable’s platform. After clients complete decisions about their life insurance policies, Abacus and its insurance affiliates will introduce them to Retirable’s licensed fiduciary advisors through warm transfers and scheduled introductions. LifeARC uses AI and 20 years of proprietary Abacus insights to generate lifespan projections.

item.title: Porch Group to acquire Allied Trust
item.description: Porch Group announced that Porch Insurance Reciprocal Exchange and Porch Group have entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Allied Trust’s insurance carrier and managing general agency, respectively. Separately, Porch Group will acquire Allied Trust’s managing general agency and captive reinsurance entity for an aggregate base purchase price of $95 million, consisting of $75 million in cash and an expected $20 million in PRCH shares. Based on Allied Trust’s expected Adjusted EBITDA (Excluding Reciprocal) contribution during the first full year following closing, the transaction represents an acquisition multiple of less than four times for Porch Group.

item.title: Evolving captives becoming strategic platforms for attracting third-party capital: Aon
item.description: Captives are rapidly evolving from risk retention vehicles into strategic capital access platforms, which in turn is beginning to attract third-party capital, according to broker Aon, who emphasises that captive owners are increasingly partnering with external investors to unlock capacity that supports growth initiatives and long-term resilience. Rather than relying exclusively on corporate capital, captive owners are partnering with external investors to unlock capacity that can support larger retention strategies, growth initiatives and resilience objectives.” Aon concludes: “Captives are evolving from risk retention vehicles into capital access platforms, helping organizations connect exposures with the most efficient mix of traditional, alternative and third-party capital.” In a recent article, the broker underscores that captives today offer much more than an opportunity to reduce insurance costs and retain risk, noting that they are now being widely used to help businesses make strategic decisions around capital deployment and long-term resilience.

item.title: Liberty Mutual Re makes sensor-triggered parametric earthquake payout in Mexico
item.description: Liberty Mutual Reinsurance (LM Re), part of Liberty Mutual Insurance Group, has issued a parametric payout to the Mexican federal government for the 7.3 magnitude earthquake that struck Mexico’s southern coast in July, and activated Safehub’s Shake Network trigger. The earthquake that struck Mexico’s southern coast on July 17th, 2026, triggered coverage under the government’s nationwide parametric earthquake and volcanic risk insurance program within weeks of the policy’s inception, for which LM Re has served as lead capacity provider of since June. Moreover, the policy utilises ShakeNet Parametric, Liberty Mutual Re’s (LM Re) earthquake parametric insurance and risk management technology solution, powered by Safehub’s Shake Network and the Global Earthquake Model’s (GEM) OpenQuake engine.

item.title: Swiss Re says increased reinsurance supply a positive, will align alt capital where it makes sense
item.description: Speaking ahead of the 2026 Baden-Baden gathering, Leopoldo Camara, Head of P&C Reinsurance Northern, Central & Eastern Europe at Swiss Re outlined that more reinsurance capital is needed in the market to address growing, interconnected risks, while also emphasising that the reinsurer will use its deep risk expertise to align alternative capital where it makes sense. And this deep risk expertise, in our view, is absolutely indispensable to arrange risk transfer in a sustainable way, to help mitigate the risk, to actually measure and quantify the risk, to develop new risk transfer approaches, and also to align alternative capital when this makes sense. “We see more capital flowing into the markets and into the reinsurance industry, and we think that is actually good news because more capital is needed to address the growing risks that we all need to deal with,” Camara explained.

item.title: Flood Re sets out plans for UK-wide flood resilience information platform
item.description: Flood Re, a joint initiative between the UK government and the insurance industry designed to improve access to affordable flood insurance for households at risk, has announced plans to expand BeFloodReady into a national platform dedicated to flood resilience. The platform is also intended to bring together research, evidence and new approaches to flood resilience, creating opportunities for policymakers, researchers, businesses, industry representatives and local communities to share information and expertise. Flood Re said that although advice and assistance on flood resilience are available from various organisations, finding relevant information and identifying appropriate measures can be difficult for individuals and communities.

item.title: Hackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges, Sparking Fires and Spoiling Food
item.description: Hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, causing fires and spoiling food . 12 a “large-scale” attack was “affecting connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France,” leading to food losses and fires. “Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented,” he wrote on X.

item.title: Bulgaria Points to Russia as Drones Hit More Cargo Ships
item.description: Bulgaria summoned Russia’s ambassador to Sofia after two ships were hit off the country’s coast, as concerns mount over the security of Black Sea shipping. 13 add to a series of more frequent attacks on ships in the western part of the Black Sea, a vital route for Ukrainian grain exports that’s close to the territorial waters of NATO member states. “There’s no logic in Ukraine destroying its own ships, and the results of these strikes work to Russia’s advantage,” Prime Minister Rumen Radev’s office said in a statement after the meeting.

item.title: Howden names reinsurance chair Richardson as group chief commercial officer
item.description: Howden has appointed Elliot Richardson to the newly created role of group chief commercial officer, putting him in charge of a new commercial strategy designed to make fuller use of the broking, reinsurance, underwriting, and employee benefits businesses the group has built. He will work with group chief financial officer Susan Panuccio and group chief operating officer David Shalders, supported by a new commercial leadership team drawn from across Howden’s regions and specialty businesses. item.title: Panda Insurtech adds pet insurance app to ChatGPT

The Panda Tierversicherung app uses details such as a pet’s species, breed, age, and size to generate illustrative, nonbinding price estimates based on PANDA’s tariff logic. The app does not issue policies, determine eligibility, or provide personalized insurance advice.

item.title: Ascend Introduces Cora, an AI Coworker Designed to Enhance Automation, Starting with Commissions Reconciliation

item.title: ILS delivers genuine diversification for alternatives allocations: Sage Advisory
item.description: Given most traditional alternative investments rely on the same economic drivers as the broader market, ILS highly differs because its returns are tied to natural catastrophe or insurance events rather than economic cycles, which leads Sage Advisory Services to say that investing in insurance-linked securities can achieve genuine diversification. However, he points out that insurance-linked securities offer investors access to a different risk premium entirely, “across a $144.5 billion market in which catastrophe bonds are the visible half and privately negotiated reinsurance is the broader one, tested on a contract calendar that does not negotiate.” “Most of what sits inside a typical alternatives allocation, whether private equity, private credit, real estate, or infrastructure, ultimately depends on the same small set of drivers. “Insurance-linked securities, or ILS, are one of the few allocations that genuinely do.

item.title: Bermuda’s BSX maintains global ILS listings leadership, takes majority of issuance through Q3
item.description: The Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX) has now listed in total 169 new catastrophe bond notes and insurance-linked securities structures in the first three-quarters of 2026, maintaining its global position as ILS listings leader and becoming home to the vast majority of listed ILS issuance so far this year. A heavy maturity load and some more early redemptions of mortgage insurance-linked notes resulted in the total value of ILS listings on the Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX) falling through the third-quarter of 2026. Having reached as high as $70.5 billion of ILS related listings on the exchange after the first-half of this year , the figure has declined slightly to almost $67.4 billion of cat bond and ILS listings on the BSX as of September 30th.

item.title: Hurricane Simon track remained outside of Mexico cat bond parametric trigger zones: Loconte
item.description: As major hurricane Simon’s path shifted west it appears to have remained offshore of the important parametric trigger zones related to the $175 million IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) catastrophe bond, according to analysis by Isacco Loconte an insurance-linked securities (ILS) Investment Specialist at asset manager Azimut Switzerland SA. As we had been reporting over the weekend , hurricane Simon’s minimum central pressure, a critical factor in determining whether any payout would come due for the catastrophe bond, did deepen to a sufficiently low level to activate a payout should the storm’s track have crossed into any of the parametric trigger boxes. While those pressure levels were strong enough to meet the L1 payout threshold for the parametric zones, the hurricane trajectory worked in the bond’s favor.” Based on the parametric trigger design, hurricane Simon’s central pressure would have needed to be at 932mb or lower to activate a payout from the zones it came closest to.

item.title: NEXROC announces intention to acquire US and Australian insurance companies
item.description: The NEXROC Group, a global investment and holding company, has announces its intention to commence tender offers for two publicly listed life insurance companies, one in the United States and one in Australia. According to the announcement, NEXROC is moving forward with the insurance acquisitions as part of the first stage of its roll-up strategy beginning next year. Under the transaction framework, both target insurers will become part of NEXROC’s insurance platform, NEXLIFE Group.

item.title: MENA reinsurers maintain top-line growth despite geopolitical and economic uncertainties: AM Best
item.description: According to the Best’s Market Segment Report, “MENA Reinsurers are Focused on Profitable Growth Opportunities Despite Heightened Geopolitical and Economic Uncertainties”, the growth potential for reinsurers is supported by adequate reinsurance pricing and emerging business opportunities, particularly in specialised risks. The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) reinsurance market continues to present solid top-line growth opportunities and attract steady inflows of international capital, even as geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainties intensify across the region, a new AM Best report states. Fleur Ngassa, financial analyst at AM Best and one of the report’s authors, said: “Despite uncertain times, some growth opportunities have emerged for reinsurers in the region.
